## Verified behavior and reasoning

The toolchain exporter requests the run and original artifact metadata through an authenticated GitHub API connection; verifies same repository, main push, completed P003/P004 workflow, run identity, publication commit, one unexpired expected toolchain artifact, finite integer size bounded at 1 GiB, and SHA-256 metadata; then downloads the original ZIP. It refuses an overlong body while reading and rejects truncated or altered bytes before creating the destination. It emits exact byte ranges, each no larger than 256 MiB, and an index with whole-archive and per-part hashes. It never unzips/rebuilds the original archive. Four parts cover its maximum accepted archive size. The index explicitly makes no phase-acceptance claim.

The failed-packaging reader requires a completed failed same-repository main-push Darling CI run. It queries all job attempts, binds each failed job to the run and head SHA, and preserves each original response byte in a gzip stream. Its raw hash, compressed hash, byte counts, and attempt identity are independently usable. Display excerpts are limited to the last 100 error matches and last 60 lines, with 4096-character truncation explicitly marked; the complete gzip content remains untruncated. A report cannot be completed if a selected download fails. Existing destination files are not overwritten.

Both workflows execute trusted main code with read-only contents/actions permissions and checkout credentials disabled. Untrusted originating run content is not executed by these readers. API tokens are attached only to GitHub API requests. The shared redirect handler rejects HTTP redirects and removes Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie across origins. Once removed, credentials do not reappear if a later redirect returns to the API host.

The version fix is at the shared packaging layer: an upstream version `0.1.YYYYMMDD` plus Debian revision `1~DISTRO` produces a valid non-native quilt version. Both source entrypoints use the same version and an orig filename based on the upstream component only. Top-level Debian packaging remains in the separate Debian tarball; nested upstream content, including nested `debian` directories, is retained. Git metadata is excluded. Binary mode retains its existing binary-build and ccache-preservation flags.

The previous workflow glob depended on the old distro-suffixed orig name and would omit the corrected archive. The collector now derives filenames from the actual changelog and checks all five source artifacts before any move. It keeps the orig archive, Debian archive, DSC, source changes, and buildinfo together. Source CI executes the fixture tests after installing packaging tools, retains the full repository `make-deb --dsc`, and fails an empty artifact upload. The binary build, source archive job, runners, and compilers were not relaxed or removed.
